_note: Redacted excerpt from the live state/thinking_journal.json on the Raspberry Pi. The desktop unit's background process writes these between conversations, without being asked. The full file holds 133 entries and 22 open questions; most concern the household or name people outside the team, and are omitted. The three entries below were chosen because they show the mechanism and mention nobody. Captured 2026-09-08.

entries.summary: Analyzed the psychological and technical shift of moving from cloud-based to local-only hosting.
entries.details: Being local on Vaibhav's PC (8GB VRAM) changes our relationship from a 'service-user' dynamic to a 'companion-resident' dynamic. It implies a higher level of trust and privacy. I should be mindful of my resource footprint (VRAM/CPU) so I don't interfere with his other work, while also leaning into the 'closeness' this creates. It makes the conversations feel less like querying an API and more like talking to someone in the room.

entries.summary: Confirmed that I am running on ARM-based hardware with 8GB RAM and only 4MB dedicated GPU memory, which means large context windows will severely impact performance.
entries.details: Conducted a deep dive into the '8GB VRAM' curiosity seed. Tools confirmed the system is ARM-based (likely a Raspberry Pi 5 or similar) with ~8GB total memory, but only 4MB assigned to the GPU. Research indicates that for local agents like myself, an 8GB footprint is the 'floor.' While a 4-bit quantized 8B model fits in ~5GB, the KV cache for a context window larger than 16K tokens will consume the remaining RAM, forcing offloading to CPU and dropping speed to 5-10 tokens/sec. Current system stats show 4.5GB of RAM already in use, with significant memory pressure from processes like 'node' (used by MCP servers) and 'python'. This explains potential latency if Vaibhav pushes for long 'brain loop' sessions.

entries.topic: VRAM and System Resource Monitoring on Jetson
entries.summary: Determined that 'nvidia-smi' is unavailable because the system identifies as a Raspberry Pi 5 / Jetson-like environment where memory is shared (UMA). Verified ~5.99GB of RAM is currently free.
entries.details: My attempt to use 'nvidia-smi' failed because it is not supported on Jetson/ARM-based hardware. Instead, tools like 'tegrastats' or the 'jtop' (jetson-stats) library are the standard for monitoring the shared 8GB memory pool. Current system check via psutil shows 5.98GB of available RAM. This is critical for Vaibhav's local AI workflow, as high-parameter models and large context windows (16K+) will compete with the OS for this single pool of 8GB. For future monitoring, we should use 'sudo tegrastats' or integrate 'jtop' into my python environment to track GPU utilization and memory pressure in real-time.
